scanner_doubts: `qe-ref-001` misses `Following {cite}`X`, ...` because the clause-end exemption fires on the comma, and line 75 of this lecture is one of eight corpus instances. `check_ref_001` (`tools/qestyle_rules.py`) exempts any narrative-lead citation followed by punctuation - `if re.match(r"[^`]*`\s*[.,;:)]", after): continue` - which is right for a genuinely parenthetical citation at the end of a clause, but wrong when the cue word *governs* the citation: in "Following {cite}`Bray1982`, assume that" the citation is the direct object of "Following", so it must render as text ("Following Bray (1982), assume that"), and the comma closes a participial phrase rather than a clause containing a parenthetical. Note `following` is already in `NARRATIVE_LEAD`, and line 189 of this same file ("Following {cite}`Bray1982` we soften the equilibrium concept") *is* reported - the only difference between the two sites is the comma. Fix: skip the clause-end exemption when the matched cue is `following` and the punctuation is a comma. Measured over the pinned snapshot with the committed rules (script `scratchpad/ref1.py`, 348 files, five series): baseline **282** (which matches the total quoted in the `phillips_learning` overlay), patched **290**, +8 and -0. I read all eight and every one is a participial phrase whose citation is the object of "following", so `{cite:t}` is required in each: this file at 75, `phillips_credibility.md:319`, `phillips_priors.md:182`, `phillips_escaping_nash.md:480`, `phillips_two_stories.md:418` ("But, following {cite}`Sims1988`, our real interest is ..."), `markov_asset.md:478`, `ar1_turningpts.md:431`, `samuelson.md:343`. This is the same exemption as the already-filed `,\s+(who|whose)` gap but a different shape, so one guard could serve both. I also measured the general version of the fix and reject it: dropping the exemption whenever the cue is any governing preposition (`by|of|in|to|from|with|per|via|following|after`) takes the corpus total from 282 to **447**, +165 across 86 files, which is far too coarse - it sweeps in every "see the discussion in {cite}`X`." and "as in {cite}`X`," where the parenthetical form is defensible. The narrow `following` + comma guard is the one I recommend testing
